paragraphs: Open Search Console using an account the business controls. Choose Domain to cover all protocols and subdomains, or URL prefix to separate a specific section such as https://www.example.com/. Domain properties require DNS verification. For URL-prefix properties, choose one of the verification methods Search Console offers.

For DNS verification, copy Google’s TXT value to the DNS provider that hosts your active nameservers. Existing TXT records can stay. After verification, open Sitemaps and submit the sitemap URL for the chosen property. A successful submission means Google could process the sitemap. Check important individual pages through URL Inspection.

If verification fails, check that the TXT record is on the correct hostname and that you edited the active DNS zone. If the sitemap cannot be fetched, open it in a private window and verify it returns XML over HTTPS. For an individual page, compare the indexed result with a live test, then check access, canonical selection and noindex before requesting recrawling.

checks: TXT record visible at authoritative nameservers
Successful fetch and intended canonical URLs
Correct property and live page accessible

paragraphs: Search Maps for your business before creating a profile. Claim an existing eligible listing through the ownership request if someone else manages it. Use the real customer-facing name and the category that describes your main activity. A service-area business should review whether its address should be visible.

Add regular and special hours, the correct website, and customer-facing phone and service details. Upload current storefront, team or product photos where useful. Follow the verification method offered in your account and use the evidence it asks for, such as signage and proof you operate the business.

Update holiday hours and test the link from mobile. If the profile is suspended, fix the underlying guideline issue and gather matching evidence before appealing. Ask customers for honest reviews without incentives. Separate calls, website visits and bookings when assessing results.

checks: Claim or request access to the right profile
Phone, hours and URL match the website
Follow the evidence requested for this profile

paragraphs: List public URLs that you want indexed and that represent the preferred version of the content. Leave redirects, missing pages, noindex URLs and duplicate filter variations out. For a large store, grouping products and collections into child sitemaps can make troubleshooting easier.

Use your CMS output if it reflects the desired indexable URLs. Check that entries use absolute URLs on the correct host and that important pages return a successful response. Supply a last-modified date only if it reflects meaningful changes to the page.

Open the live sitemap and submit it through Search Console. Review the fetch status, then inspect a sample of important pages. Sitemap inclusion supports discovery, while internal links and page quality still matter. If URLs are missing after a migration, verify the new sitemap is being generated from the production site.

checks: Reachable at the submitted HTTPS address
Inspect representative product and service URLs

paragraphs: Google can discover a URL through links or a sitemap, fetch it later, and decide whether it belongs in the index. There is no fixed timetable. A recrawl request can help Google revisit a page, but the request alone does not determine when or whether the page appears.

In URL Inspection, compare the indexed information with a live test. Check that the page returns a successful response and that Google can see its primary content. Review noindex rules, redirects and the selected canonical, especially when the page looks similar to another URL.

Link to the page from relevant indexed sections and include it in the sitemap if it is a preferred public URL. Resolve duplicate or thin content at the template level. Keep a record of the fix and check a representative sample over time instead of repeatedly requesting the same URL.

checks: Link from a relevant public page
Confirm access and rendered primary content
Compare preferred and selected canonical URLs

paragraphs: SEO focuses on discovery and visibility in unpaid search. AEO is a shorthand for making answers easy to identify and use. GEO is a shorthand for improving the chance that a generative experience can find, interpret or cite useful material. The labels overlap, and platforms can implement these experiences differently.

Publish a clear answer backed by evidence. Put the method, author, limits and date close to claims that depend on them. Keep material in accessible HTML and make related pages easy to find. Google says its AI search features build on its general SEO practices.

Track qualified organic visits and conversions as usual. Where referrals are identifiable, compare them separately. Sample the questions customers actually ask and track whether your pages are referenced. Treat mentions, clicks and revenue as distinct measures.

checks: Make the answer clear and cite the evidence
Sample citations and track verifiable referrals

paragraphs: List the task the page serves, the questions visitors bring, and the next action they should be able to take. Choose a descriptive page title and main heading. A service page should quickly explain scope and eligibility; a guide should answer the question with enough detail to be useful.

Add internal links from genuinely relevant pages with descriptive anchor text. Check the preferred URL and indexing controls. Give useful images accurate alt text. Keep prices, specifications or service areas visible as text where customers need them.

Read the mobile page through to its primary action, then inspect the live URL and record the release date. Review impressions, clicks and conversions for that page. If it gains visibility for the wrong searches, revisit the copy and intent rather than adding more variations of the same keyword.

checks: Audit link paths, canonical and index status
Test the main action on a phone

paragraphs: Register the domain in a business account and choose a host with backups, SSL and a staging option you can manage. Install WordPress through the host or manually. Keep a separate administrator account and record who owns the domain, hosting, and recovery access.

Choose a maintained theme and decide whether the block editor meets your needs. Build a home page, essential service or product pages, and a contact path. Set typography, navigation and styles centrally. Add plugins only for specific gaps and check whether their features duplicate hosting or theme functions.

Update components, test the form and recovery procedure, then check mobile and keyboard navigation. Confirm the intended URLs are publicly available and the sitemap reflects them. Where replacing a site, map redirects from the old URLs before switching the domain.

checks: Test the theme with real content lengths
Test forms, redirects and public access

paragraphs: For WordPress projects, compare managed options such as WP Engine, Kinsta, Pressable and Flywheel with broader providers such as SiteGround, Bluehost, DreamHost, Hostinger, Namecheap and Cloudways. These ten candidates serve different needs. Check current renewal terms and which features apply to the specific plan.

Give higher weight to the problems your team cannot handle alone. Compare backup retention and restoration, staging, support hours, region choices, migration help, and resource limits. Add the costs of backups, email, security or CDN services that the base plan omits.

Use the same site copy and a similar traffic pattern to check performance. Ask support how it handles a restore or failed deployment. Document DNS and mail records, take an export you can restore, and keep the old host available until the new site has been verified.

checks: Compare total cost over two years
Ask who handles migration and recoveries

paragraphs: Choose a design that suits your content, then build the service, contact and trust pages first. Write navigation labels in customer language. Use reusable sections and a consistent type scale rather than recreating layouts page by page.

Confirm where the domain is managed and follow the connection steps shown in Squarespace. Keep any existing email records in place. Set descriptive SEO titles for important pages, add meaningful image text, and inspect the generated sitemap after publication.

Open the site on mobile, submit an enquiry and check where it arrives. Verify redirects if replacing a site. Test the canonical hostname and remove any launch restrictions that should no longer apply. Measure contact or purchase completions separately from general visits.

checks: Use customer language rather than internal labels
Verify enquiry delivery and sitemap URLs

paragraphs: Identify the pages that repeat, such as projects, services and locations. Put reusable fields into CMS collections. Create sample entries with long titles and missing optional fields so the template is tested against realistic content.

Create reusable components and check breakpoints from the smallest practical viewport upward. Use semantic headings and accessible form labels. Set titles and descriptions for static and collection pages, and manage which URLs should appear in the sitemap.

Confirm the primary domain, redirects, mobile navigation and form delivery. Inspect a collection page in Search Console after launch. If moving from another CMS, use a URL inventory and compare old and new paths before changing DNS.

checks: Test entries with missing optional fields
Check navigation and forms below desktop widths
Map valuable old paths to relevant replacements

paragraphs: Choose an editor and design suited to the content. Build the main service, product and contact pages, then make pricing or booking details easy to find. Check the mobile layout before cloning a template or adding more pages.

Connect the correct domain, review the SEO setup for important pages, and verify the property in Search Console. Check the generated sitemap and whether the URLs people should discover are included. Add apps for clearly defined needs and test their effect on loading and forms.

Test mobile navigation, enquiry notifications and booking or checkout flows. Inspect the published domain without being logged in. If moving from an earlier site, test redirects for the URLs that brought customers or had incoming links.

checks: Finish a booking or enquiry on a narrow screen
Check the live sitemap and property
Remove tools with no clear business purpose

paragraphs: Design the home and one high-priority conversion page before expanding the site. Reuse navigation, buttons and layout sections. For a recurring content type, define CMS fields and test long entries, narrow screens and missing images.

Give important pages descriptive titles and summaries. Confirm the domain and preferred hostname, then check responsive image sizes, forms and keyboard navigation. Review whether embeds or animations delay the main content.

Publish, test enquiries, and inspect the live page rather than relying on the editor preview. Check mobile loading and whether key pages are discoverable through links. Keep a list of settings that must be recreated if the site is ever moved to another platform.

checks: Update navigation once and check affected pages
Record content, URL and domain ownership

paragraphs: Start by deciding which plan fits the store you want to build. Compare the permanent subscription, billing period and required features before accepting a trial offer. You can choose a provisional plan now and activate it after creating the account; researching a plan does not require paying first.

The table below records the US-dollar list prices displayed on Shopify’s US pricing page on 29 November 2026. Annual figures are monthly equivalents billed yearly. Taxes, payment processing, third-party transaction charges, apps, domains and paid themes can add costs. Regional prices, promotions and availability can change, so confirm the checkout total.
steps: Open Shopify’s pricing page and set your actual business region.
Compare Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus against your team access, shipping and operational requirements.
Record both monthly billing and the annual commitment, then choose the lowest plan that meets your launch needs.

table.caption: Shopify online-store plans: US list prices checked 29 November 2026
rows: Small team; up to 5 staff accounts
Larger operations; up to 15 staff accounts

sections.note: Starter is not available to new stores according to Shopify’s current Help Center. It is not a substitute for the full theme-and-collection store described in this guide. POS Pro is an additional retail product, not a replacement for your online-store plan.

paragraphs: Now create the account that owns the store. Use an email address the business controls rather than an agency employee’s personal address. Keep ownership and recovery access with the merchant, even when a developer will do the build.

Shopify can show different onboarding screens by country, account and offer. Follow the available account-creation method, then complete or skip the optional questionnaire. The important outcome is access to the correct store’s admin, not matching every question in a screenshot.
steps: Visit shopify.com and select Start for free.
Create an account with your business email and a unique password, or use an available sign-in provider. Verify the email if prompted.
Enter truthful country and business details. Add billing now or use the available skip option.
Complete or skip the setup questions, open the admin and record the store’s original myshopify.com identifier.
sections.note: Do not create a store in another country merely to unlock a payment provider. The business, banking and verification information must match your real setup.

paragraphs: Your account and your subscription are separate decisions. Creating an account gets you into the admin; choosing a paid plan determines the recurring bill and capabilities. Recheck the plan once you can see the actual offer attached to your store.

For an example launch budget, write three headings in a spreadsheet: fixed monthly costs, one-time setup costs and costs per order. Keep payment fees and shipping outside the platform subscription line. This prevents a low introductory price from becoming your entire operating budget.
steps: Open Settings > Plan, or the plan-selection prompt shown in the admin.
Select the plan researched in step 1 and compare monthly versus yearly billing.
Read the introductory offer, renewal price, billing date, currency and cancellation conditions before confirming.
Add an authorized billing method and save the invoice details for your accounts team.

paragraphs: Configure the store before designing it. The legal business, customer-facing contact information, currency, time zone and weight units influence checkout, reporting and fulfillment. Confirm these with whoever runs the business, rather than guessing from the market you hope to reach.

Make a small access register: owner, developer, fulfillment lead and finance contact. Record what each person needs, not their passwords. Use individual access and two-step authentication where available. Remove temporary access after the handover.
steps: Open Settings > General and review the store name, legal details, business contact information, time zone and default units.
Choose the store currency deliberately before transactions start, and review Shopify’s rules before changing it later.
Secure the owner account, save recovery information and invite staff or collaborators with appropriate permissions.
Keep the storefront private while it is unfinished; use the available password or visibility controls.

paragraphs: A domain is the address customers remember; a theme is the design they see. You can plan the address before buying it, and you can build on the temporary Shopify address while availability and ownership are checked. The custom domain does not replace the store’s underlying account identifier.

Shortlist three names that can be spoken clearly and typed without explanation. For a fictional homeware brand, compare a clear brand-led name with a long string of product keywords. Prefer the one customers can remember, then check for confusingly similar brands, renewal costs and suitable social handles.
steps: Write down the brand spelling and the countries you intend to serve.
Check domain availability through Shopify or a registrar; compare renewal pricing as well as the first year.
Check whether the name could confuse customers with another business.
Register it in an account controlled by your business and document renewal ownership.

paragraphs: If you buy through Shopify, use Settings > Domains and the purchase flow. If you already own the name, connect it from the same area and follow the instructions for your DNS provider. Connecting a domain and transferring its registration are different operations; you do not need to transfer it just to use it with Shopify.

For a third-party connection, follow the record values shown in Shopify and its current provider guide. Preserve unrelated email records. Wait for the domain status and TLS certificate to become ready before treating the address as live. Avoid repeatedly changing DNS while propagation is in progress.
steps: In Settings > Domains, choose Buy new domain or Connect existing domain as appropriate.
For an existing domain, enter the root name without a page path and follow automatic connection if your provider supports it.
If manual setup is required, update the specified A, AAAA and www CNAME records at the DNS provider. Keep MX and email-verification records intact.
Return to Shopify to verify connection, select the intended primary domain and check that alternate addresses redirect correctly.

images.alt: Shopify Domains screen showing Connect existing domain
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. Shopify Domains screen showing Connect existing domain.

images.alt: Shopify dialog for entering an existing domain name
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. Shopify dialog for entering an existing domain name.

images.alt: Shopify domain connection status and TLS certificate checks
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. Shopify domain connection status and TLS certificate checks.

paragraphs: Choose from real themes in the Shopify Theme Store rather than an unlicensed ZIP download. Test a theme with your product photos, longest product title and likely collection size. A demo is a starting point: it does not prove your own photography, menu or checkout will work.

Use the shortlist below as a comparison set, not a promise that one theme fits every business. Free themes can be a sensible launch choice. A paid theme is worth considering when its built-in layout saves custom work you actually need. Confirm the current license, features and price on the linked listing.
steps: Open the Shopify Theme Store and filter by price and the features your catalog needs.
Preview a product, collection, menu, cart and mobile view in each candidate.
Score navigation clarity, product media, filtering needs, text length and accessibility with your real content.
Choose one primary candidate and one backup; reserve any paid-theme budget before customization.

table.caption: A theme shortlist to test with your own products
rows: Flexible storefront sections and product presentation
Minimal layout and image-led product pages
Premium editorial presentation; verify needed features
Merchandising and promotion layouts; verify needed features

images.alt: Horizon desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store
images.caption: Official Shopify theme preview. Horizon desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store.

images.alt: Dawn desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store
images.caption: Official Shopify theme preview. Dawn desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store.

images.alt: Craft desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store
images.caption: Official Shopify theme preview. Craft desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store.

images.alt: Sense desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store
images.caption: Official Shopify theme preview. Sense desktop theme preview from the Shopify Theme Store.

paragraphs: The account includes a default theme, but it does not have to become your final design. Work on an unpublished theme while checking content and navigation. If you are redesigning an existing store, first duplicate the live theme and record what must be preserved.

A theme is not your entire store database. Switching a theme changes presentation and settings; it does not substitute for product, payment and fulfillment setup. Keep a change log so you can identify which customizations belong to the theme and which belong to apps or store configuration.
steps: Go to Online Store > Themes and open the free-theme or Theme Store options available in your admin.
Add a free theme, or use the paid listing’s trial option to add a preview.
Open the theme editor and preview desktop and mobile before editing.
Purchase a paid theme before publishing it, and keep its license assigned to the correct store.
sources: Add, preview and buy a theme

paragraphs: Set a coherent visual system before filling every section. Choose a readable body font, heading hierarchy, button style and restrained color palette. A store should still make sense when an image fails or a customer uses keyboard navigation.

Create a simple content kit: logo, favicon, two or three brand colors, product image guidelines, heading examples and button wording. For a fictional kitchenware store, “Shop cookware” tells a shopper more than “Discover more.” Use real product benefits instead of decorative slogans in every section.
steps: In Online Store > Themes, open the editor using Edit theme or Customize, depending on the interface shown.
Use Theme settings for brand colors, typography, logo and global styling.
Select the Home page template and use sections and blocks to build the first layout.
Preview narrow, tablet and desktop sizes; test contrast, image cropping, focus states and button labels.

images.alt: Shopify online store editor displaying the Dawn theme and its page sections
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. The Dawn editor example illustrates sections; your theme and labels can differ.

paragraphs: Give the homepage one clear job: help the right visitor understand the offer and reach a useful collection or product. A large carousel is optional. A clear first screen, dependable menu and visible shipping information often help more than filling the page with movement.

Sketch the page as a journey: introduction, main collections, selected products, useful evidence, delivery reassurance and help. For each block, write the next action. If two sections repeat the same message without helping a decision, combine them.
steps: Add a concise first heading that explains what you sell and for whom.
Link the main call to action to a relevant collection, not an empty page.
Add featured collections and a small set of representative products after the products are ready.
Include genuine information about materials, delivery, returns and support. Publish reviews only when they are authentic.
After completing steps 12–15, return to the preview and verify every button and menu destination.
sections.note: Build the draft layout now. Populate and verify product and collection links after steps 12–15, when those resources exist. Keep the store private until the launch checks pass.

paragraphs: Before checkout is opened, customers need to understand who sells the products and what happens after payment. Add an About page, a working Contact page, delivery information and the policies relevant to your business. Do not publish placeholder promises.

Policy templates need review. Match the refund window, delivery process, address and support contact to the business that will actually fulfill orders. Ask a qualified adviser about market-specific legal requirements; a generated policy is not a compliance guarantee.
steps: Create informational pages through Online Store > Pages, or the page area shown in your admin.
Write About, Contact and delivery content with real business details.
Open Settings > Policies and review return/refund, privacy, terms and shipping content.
Check translated policies if you sell in more than one language.
Link customer-help pages and policies from the footer, then submit a test contact enquiry.

paragraphs: Only now, after the account and storefront foundation exist, start building the catalog. Complete one representative product before importing hundreds. Use that product to test descriptions, images, options and the product-page layout.

Write information that removes buying uncertainty: what the item is, materials, dimensions, what is included, care instructions and delivery expectations. For a fictional ceramic mug, give its capacity and dishwasher guidance rather than repeating “premium quality” in every sentence.
steps: Go to Products > Add product. Enter a clear name and an original description.
Upload accurate product media and set a real selling price; check that no unintended zero-price item can be purchased.
Assign the appropriate product category, relevant attributes and shipping requirements.
Use product fields or metafields for consistent specifications where appropriate.
Save as a draft, preview the page and check it on a phone before making it available on the intended sales channel.

paragraphs: Use variants for genuine choices such as size or color. Do not duplicate a product page merely because the same shirt comes in three sizes. Give each sellable variation a consistent identifier and verify its own price, image and availability.

Inventory belongs to a real fulfillment process. Decide who counts stock, which location dispatches orders and how returns are put back into stock. A neat product page cannot compensate for selling units that are not available.
steps: Open the product and add the option names and values customers need.
Review every generated variant; assign a SKU, relevant barcode, price, weight and image as appropriate.
Create or verify the stock location and enter counted quantities.
Choose the out-of-stock behavior deliberately; allow continued selling only when your preorder or backorder process supports it.
For a large catalog, test a small CSV import, export a backup and check the result before uploading the rest.

paragraphs: Collections are shopping destinations. Group products around categories customers understand, such as dinnerware or linen shirts, then give each collection a distinct purpose. Avoid creating dozens of thin pages just to repeat nearby keywords.

Plan a small collection map before building rules. In a fictional homeware store, “Dining” can lead to “Mugs” and “Dinner plates.” A seasonal gift collection may serve a different need. Check that every collection has enough relevant products to deserve a permanent navigation link.
steps: Go to Products > Collections and create the first collection.
Add a descriptive title, useful introduction and suitable image.
Choose the manual product selection or automatic conditions available in your admin.
Review the actual matched products, including variant behavior, and remove irrelevant items.
Set a sensible sort order, preview the collection and make it available to the intended channel.

paragraphs: The store is not ready if good pages can only be found through a direct URL. Connect the homepage, main menu, collections, product pages and help pages so shoppers can move between them naturally.

Use a short menu that names categories clearly. Test with a task: “Find a blue medium shirt, check delivery and contact support.” Watch where the shopper hesitates. Fix the labels and destinations before adding more filters or promotional banners.
steps: Open Content > Menus and edit the main menu.
Add links to the most important collections and information pages using Shopify’s resource picker.
Assign the menu to the theme header and the policy/help menu to the footer.
Configure collection filters supported by the theme and Shopify Search & Discovery where needed.
Test mobile menus, search, empty results and breadcrumbs if your theme includes them.

paragraphs: Choose payment methods that are available to your business location and product category. Shopify Payments eligibility depends on supported countries and verification. If it is unavailable, evaluate compatible third-party providers and their settlement terms.

Do not assume that a gateway available to a US merchant can be activated by a Pakistan-based business. Check the business documents, receiving bank, settlement currency, refunds and total fees. Cash on delivery and manual methods also need an operational process, not just a checkout toggle.
steps: Open Settings > Payments and review the providers available to your store.
Complete the selected provider’s genuine identity, business and bank verification.
Review transaction charges, payout timing, refund handling and supported currencies.
Choose automatic or manual payment capture according to the fulfillment process.
Use the provider’s supported test method before accepting real customer orders.

paragraphs: Shipping must match the items and regions you can actually fulfill. Configure packages, origins and delivery options before advertising worldwide delivery. A customer should see a usable rate for a supported address and a clear restriction for an unsupported one.

Build a basket matrix: one light item, multiple items, an oversized item and a free-shipping threshold. Check costs and margins for each. If the parcel costs more to send than the order contributes, the rate needs work before launch.
steps: Open Settings > Shipping and delivery. Confirm the fulfillment origin and packages.
Create shipping zones for supported destinations and set suitable flat, free or calculated rates.
Use separate profiles where products need different rules.
Enter correct product and package weights, then test representative postcodes and basket values.
Write delivery estimates that your courier and operations team can support.

paragraphs: Tax settings should follow the business’s actual registrations and selling obligations. Shopify can help calculate taxes, but calculation settings do not decide where you must register, file or remit.

Prepare a configuration brief for your accountant: business location, fulfillment locations, product categories and customer markets. Ask which settings and registrations apply. Keep that advice with the launch checklist instead of copying another store’s rates.
steps: Open Settings > Taxes and duties and review the regions in which you sell.
Enter registrations only when they apply to your business.
Review whether displayed prices include or exclude tax and how shipping is treated.
Check a representative checkout calculation with your adviser.
Document who reviews tax changes and reporting after launch.

paragraphs: Start with the markets you can support properly. Currency display, payment acceptance, translated copy, stock availability, duties and customer service need to agree. A language selector alone does not make a store ready for international orders.

For each market, write down the customer promise: what can be bought, how it is priced, how long it takes and who helps. Translate size information, delivery details and checkout messages, not just the homepage.
steps: Open Markets and review the default and proposed customer regions.
Configure supported countries, product availability and the localization features your plan and payment setup allow.
Add reviewed translations and regional content where needed.
Test a full order from each priority region, including currency, address and shipping restrictions.
Avoid duplicate regional pages unless they provide a genuine local experience.

paragraphs: Install an app when a specific requirement is not covered by the platform or theme. Typical needs might include subscriptions, reviews, returns or back-in-stock messages. Do not start by installing a long “must-have” list.

Keep an app register with the purpose, owner, recurring fee, permissions and removal process. If two apps add the same pixel, review widget or SEO markup, decide which one owns that function. This makes troubleshooting and handover much easier.
steps: Write the requirement and check whether Shopify or the chosen theme already handles it.
Compare compatible apps, current pricing, support and requested permissions.
Test on a theme copy where possible and measure storefront performance.
Review the generated storefront content and event tracking for conflicts.
Remove unused app embeds and follow the developer’s cleanup instructions after uninstalling.

paragraphs: Shopify supplies useful infrastructure, but visibility still depends on useful pages, crawl access and relevance. Give different searches a suitable destination: a product for an exact item, a collection for a category, and a guide for a research question.

Create a keyword-to-page map. For our fictional homeware store, “stoneware mugs” belongs to a useful collection, a specific model belongs to its product page, and “how to care for stoneware” belongs to a guide. Link the guide to relevant products. Avoid forcing all three searches onto the homepage.
steps: List your main products, categories and customer questions.
Group searches by intent rather than assigning a new page to every variation.
Map one primary purpose to each product, collection and informational page.
Write unique helpful copy, then link related collections, products and guides together.
Review the map when actual Search Console queries become available.

paragraphs: Edit the search engine listing on important products, collections and pages. Describe the actual offer and use natural language. Give a collection a category-focused title and a product a specific name; do not paste the same metadata across the store.

Example: “Stoneware Mugs | Everyday Kitchenware” is clearer than a list of unrelated keywords. A description can explain capacity, availability and delivery without promising facts the page cannot support. Search engines may choose different snippets, so metadata is an input rather than a guaranteed display.
steps: Open a product or collection and find its Search engine listing or Website SEO preview.
Edit the title, description and URL handle carefully; keep established URLs unless a change has a clear benefit.
Check the homepage metadata in the online-store preferences area.
Write alt text that explains the image’s useful content, such as the item and visible detail.
Check the page’s visible main heading and use subheadings to organize specifications and buying information.

paragraphs: A product may be reachable through several paths or variants. Inspect the rendered page before adding an SEO app that rewrites its canonical. Shopify themes should expose the appropriate canonical URL, but custom code and apps need checking.

For a migration, make a spreadsheet of old URLs and their closest replacements. Keep useful product URLs stable. Do not redirect every discontinued item to the homepage: use a genuine substitute or leave a helpful unavailable page where appropriate.
steps: Open representative product and collection pages and inspect the HTML canonical link.
Check that important pages point to the intended live HTTPS address.
When changing a handle, enable or create the appropriate redirect and test the old URL.
Manage redirects through Content > Menus > URL redirects, or the redirect area shown in your admin.
Check duplicate descriptions, broken internal links and filter URLs before creating broad indexation rules.

paragraphs: Shopify generates a sitemap automatically. Once the store is publicly accessible, use the canonical domain’s /sitemap.xml address. Submitting it helps search engines discover pages; it does not guarantee inclusion or a ranking date.

Keep the distinction between access and ranking clear. A private storefront, a noindex instruction, a failed page or an unexpected canonical needs investigation. Repeated sitemap submissions do not replace fixing the underlying issue.
steps: Verify the correct domain in Google Search Console, using a supported verification method.
After launch, open https://your-domain.example/sitemap.xml and confirm that it loads. Replace this example with your real address.
Submit sitemap.xml in the Sitemaps report and review its processing status.
Inspect the homepage, one collection and one product; review live accessibility and Google’s selected canonical.
Use Bing Webmaster Tools for Bing visibility and monitor indexing reports over time.
sections.note: Verify domain ownership now. Complete the public sitemap, live URL and indexability checks after step 29. A private or password-protected store is not ready for public crawling.

paragraphs: Product structured data describes information such as name, price, currency and availability. Check what the theme and apps already output before adding another source. The markup must match what a customer can actually see and buy.

If you use Google Merchant Center, keep feed data and the store synchronized. A product being published in Shopify is not the same as being approved for every shopping destination. Check diagnostics and policy issues rather than assuming that a feed submission is complete.
steps: Run representative product URLs through Google’s Rich Results Test.
Check Product and Offer data against the selected product, currency, price and stock state.
Use genuine reviews only; do not add invented aggregate ratings to obtain stars.
Configure the supported Google & YouTube channel if it suits your market and requirements, then review Merchant Center diagnostics.
Retest markup after changing themes or review apps.

paragraphs: A heavy theme, oversized media and overlapping apps can slow an otherwise sound store. Test the actual product and collection templates, not just an empty homepage. Check performance after each major feature is added.

Make performance part of the design: reserve space for images, avoid autoplay media above the fold, keep text readable and make controls usable by keyboard. Compress images without destroying detail. A product photo should still let a shopper judge the item.
steps: Review Shopify’s web-performance reports and use PageSpeed Insights on representative URLs.
Resize source media sensibly and use the theme’s responsive image handling.
Remove unused app embeds, redundant pixels and unnecessary sliders.
Check loading, interaction and layout stability on mobile; distinguish lab tests from real-user data.
Test keyboard navigation, visible focus, labels and alt text before sign-off.

paragraphs: Measure the journey you want to improve: product view, add to cart, checkout and purchase. Choose one supported implementation for each analytics destination, and check it before adding another app or theme script.

Use a test log with order ID, value, currency and observed events. Compare the completed order with the event report, accounting for consent choices and test-mode exclusions. Two purchase events for one order can make advertising appear more profitable than it is.
steps: Review Shopify analytics first and decide which extra measurement tools you need.
Connect GA4 through a supported Shopify integration such as the Google & YouTube channel when available for your setup.
Configure customer privacy and consent settings for your markets.
Test permitted customer events and check that purchase tracking is not duplicated.
Keep an event map and record the owner of every pixel or integration.
sections.note: Prepare analytics now, then validate live collection after step 29. Shopify’s GA4 documentation says analytics cannot track events while the store remains in private mode; simulated test orders are not a live-sales measurement check.

paragraphs: A store is not ready because its homepage looks finished. Test the full journey, including payment failure, delivery options, order emails, stock changes and cancellation or refund handling. Use supported test facilities rather than making accidental customer charges.

Write the expected outcome first. For a two-item basket, record the variant choices, subtotal, shipping and expected stock reduction. After the test, compare each result. If the totals or notifications differ, fix the cause before launch.
steps: Choose a paid plan, then enable the supported test gateway or Shopify Payments test mode.
Place successful and unsuccessful test orders using the provider’s documented test details.
Check product variants, discounts, shipping addresses, taxes, emails and order processing.
Test cancellation, refund and fulfillment procedures with the team.
Turn test mode off and remove accidental sample products or test settings before accepting customers.

images.alt: Shopify checkout example shown on desktop and mobile
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. Shopify checkout example shown on desktop and mobile.

paragraphs: Launch when the merchant, payments and fulfillment teams can support real orders. Publishing a theme and making the store public are separate checks. Review the visibility controls shown in your admin and confirm that customers can reach checkout.

Use an incognito browser and mobile data for the final check. Review the primary domain, menu, product details, customer contact route and payment availability. Keep a rollback plan for the theme and nominate a person to watch the first orders.
steps: Confirm the chosen theme is published and the custom domain is ready.
Turn off test payments and verify the real provider’s status.
Open the online-store visibility or preferences area and remove password/private access when the launch checklist is complete.
Visit the public store without an admin session and check representative pages and checkout.
Submit the public sitemap, check analytics and begin promotion only after the buying journey works.

paragraphs: Launch begins the operating phase. Assign responsibility for orders, returns, inventory, content and site changes. Keep the same checklist when a new app, market, theme or payment method is introduced.

Review customer questions as content opportunities. If several buyers ask about sizing or delivery, improve the relevant page and verify whether the answer reduces confusion. For SEO, compare useful search impressions, qualified visits and sales rather than celebrating any increase in raw traffic.
steps: Daily: review failed payments, support enquiries, unfulfilled orders and stock anomalies.
Weekly: check broken links, key search queries, collection quality and conversion issues.
Monthly: review apps and costs, test checkout and prioritize content improvements.
Before a theme update, duplicate the current theme and test the draft against product, cart and app requirements.
Keep a handover record of domains, access, integrations and operational owners.

images.alt: Shopify theme update dialog showing the option to add a new version
images.caption: Official Shopify reference screenshot. Shopify theme update dialog showing the option to add a new version.

checks: Correct plan, billing and merchant-owned account
Live HTTPS domain, usable theme and navigation
Accurate products, variants, images and stock
Useful metadata, crawl access and verified tracking
Test orders passed, public access and real payments ready

paragraphs: Choose hosting that can handle checkout, backups and updates. Install WooCommerce and set the store location, currency, shipping and payments. Assign clear responsibility for maintaining the software and restoring the store if a release breaks it.

Use sensible categories and clear product attributes. Test variation selection, shipping combinations, taxes and receipts with representative orders. Provide useful product details so shoppers can compare options without leaving the page.

Test refunds, cancelled orders and failed payments before launch. Confirm product and category indexing, redirects, and any schema output. Run a real test order where appropriate and reconcile events against the store’s records.

checks: Document fulfilment, shipping and payment decisions
Run paid, declined and cancelled scenarios
Inspect schema and index visibility after publication

paragraphs: Segment conversion rates by device, landing page and traffic source before drawing conclusions. Test the path yourself from arrival to confirmation. Compare analytics with support questions, search terms and usability sessions to understand what visitors could not find.

If mobile visitors often leave after seeing a quote form, test whether removing fields the sales team never uses helps qualified submissions. Define a primary metric, quality guardrail, and test duration before changing the page. For low traffic, use usability testing and note the limits of before-and-after comparisons.

Track completed orders or qualified enquiries alongside conversion rate. A shorter form that doubles submissions while reducing qualified leads can make sales less efficient. Document results and watch for changes in traffic mix before rolling the test across the site.

checks: Choose a primary metric and quality guardrail
Verify downstream lead or order quality

paragraphs: Paid search can help test an offer or reach people quickly while you have budget. Organic search builds discoverable pages over time. Use ads to test commercial demand and SEO to improve the pages and information that customers can find independently.

Budget paid media, management and landing-page work together. For SEO, count content, development, reporting and maintenance. A lower cost per click has little meaning if visitors rarely qualify or purchase. Separate branded searches from campaigns aimed at new prospects.

Give both channels an agreed conversion definition. Use search-term findings to improve service pages and send paid visitors to suitable landing pages. Check for overlap using conversion paths and, when practical, controlled experiments. Avoid crediting the same sale twice.

checks: Test a specific offer with paid search
Strengthen the pages users can find organically

paragraphs: Calculate revenue after discounts and refunds, then subtract variable costs such as product, fulfilment and payment fees. If an order contributes 40 before advertising, 40 is the approximate break-even acquisition cost before other costs. Include management and creative costs when assessing the programme.

For a lead campaign, estimate the share that qualifies and the share of qualified leads that buys. If ten leads cost 250 and one customer contributes 400 before marketing, the campaign has 150 left before overhead. Small samples can swing sharply, so review a longer period.

Reconcile platform reports with transaction IDs and CRM outcomes. Distinguish new from returning customers and delayed purchases from immediate ones. Adjust attribution windows and refund treatment consistently before comparing campaigns.

Choose the objective based on the result you can measure, such as a purchase or a qualified lead. Review available Advantage+ controls, placements and audience settings in your account. Features and defaults can vary by objective and account. Review Meta’s live product documentation before changing your setup. In June 2026, Meta announced that its “About this ad” interface would show AI labels for ads created or significantly edited with its generative tools. Review creative and disclosure settings before campaign approval.

Build ads around distinct customer problems, proof points and objections. Change a meaningful variable at a time where possible. Keep a record of message, format and destination page so a useful result can be repeated.

Review Pixel and Conversions API events where applicable and use consistent event IDs for deduplication. Compare ad reporting with actual leads, sales and refunds. Evaluate the campaign against its cost and lead quality, and document attribution settings before comparing periods.

checks: Optimise for a measurable business outcome
Check event duplication and attribution settings

paragraphs: Use the first screen to state who the page is for, what the offer includes, and what visitors can do next. If an ad promises a fixed-price audit, make the price, scope and eligibility easy to confirm on the page.

Use genuine examples, clear deliverables, relevant testimonials and practical details such as timing or cancellation terms. Place supporting evidence near the claim it backs up. Keep forms short and explain how sensitive details will be used when they are needed.

Run the page on a phone and through keyboard navigation. Submit the form, check the confirmation, and verify that the lead reaches the right team. Compare qualified conversion counts by source and adjust the offer, message or form based on what you learn.

checks: Match the promise in the ad or search
Test confirmation and delivery from a phone

paragraphs: Choose events that describe actual business behaviour. Use generate_lead for a successfully recorded enquiry and purchase for a completed transaction. Agree on what qualifies as a lead and which event represents a key outcome. Avoid including personal information in analytics parameters.

Use DebugView and complete an actual test journey. Confirm events fire once, and send a unique transaction ID with purchases. Check value and currency against store records and account for consent, redirects and payment hops that can affect attribution.

Look at landing pages and channels in the context of qualified leads, refunds and revenue. Record discrepancies and their likely causes before comparing campaigns. Give teams the same time zone, attribution assumptions and event definitions.

checks: Send after the enquiry is accepted
Send one transaction ID with value and currency
Check analytics against CRM and order data

paragraphs: Confirm what counts as a primary conversion and whether it genuinely matches the account’s objective. Test form, call and purchase tracking. Review conversion windows, duplicate events and whether campaigns optimise for a meaningful outcome.

Review search terms, targeting, locations, match types and ads by campaign objective. Look for irrelevant terms and separate brand demand from new-customer campaigns. Compare traffic and cost with actual lead or order quality, not just click volume.

Fix measurement or major leakage before testing creative. Record the date, campaign and hypothesis for each change. Leave enough observation time to judge a decision, particularly when sales take days or weeks to close.

checks: Inspect actual search terms and location settings

paragraphs: Build neighbourhood and property-type pages around real questions, with current listings, useful local details and clear search paths. Write distinct copy where locations differ and link from area guides to relevant listings as they become available.

Keep availability, prices and viewing information current. Give important listing or development pages stable URLs and useful photos. Decide what to do when a property is sold based on whether the page retains valuable information.

Measure calls, viewing requests and qualified leads. Use local profiles only where the business qualifies. Compare areas and listing types by enquiry quality and follow-up outcomes rather than rankings alone.

checks: Offer real neighbourhood or property detail
Keep availability and viewing information current

paragraphs: Clear service and location pages help patients find relevant information over time. Paid campaigns may reach people quickly in targeted areas, subject to platform policies and applicable rules. Compare both based on suitable appointments and capacity.

Make practitioners, services, address, hours and next steps clear. Have an appropriate reviewer check medical content. Make appointment instructions accessible and treat patient details carefully when setting up analytics or ad measurement.

Track call and booking completions rather than visits alone. Use appropriately configured reporting that avoids exposing patient information. If enquiries rise but appointments do not, check availability, call handling and the match between the service and campaign.

checks: Verify services, hours and booking details
Check capacity and relevant campaign rules
Compare bookings without exposing patient data

paragraphs: A U.S. resident business selling remote customer support to a non-U.S. customer may be supplying a U.S. service export. A U.S. company buying support from a provider abroad is generally importing the service from its perspective. The caller’s location alone does not determine the transaction direction.

Remote delivery is one way to supply services across borders. Sales through a foreign affiliate can be measured separately. For a multi-entity contract, establish who contracts, who pays and which entities operate in the countries involved.

Set expectations for resolution time, handoffs, quality review and peak coverage. Separate contact volume from resolved issues and document who owns data access, escalation and reporting. A shared definition of a resolved case helps both organisations compare performance.

checks: Distinguish remote supply from an affiliate sale
Agree on escalation and resolution definitions

paragraphs: Cover individual use cases, integrations, switching costs and comparisons prospects actually ask about. Include screenshots and requirements where useful. A broad traffic topic earns its place when it can lead naturally to a relevant product page or buying decision.

Explain who the product works for, what the demo covers and how prospects should prepare. Offer a relevant CTA for the page rather than asking every reader to book immediately. Make the form and scheduling experience easy to use on mobile.

Track demos through qualification and opportunity creation. Separate signing into an existing account from genuine acquisition. Use sales notes to identify gaps in content and judge whether a high-traffic page attracts the buyers the product can serve.

checks: Build real use-case and integration pages
Explain what the prospect should expect
Separate trial users, new prospects and existing accounts

paragraphs: Use useful category names, distinct page titles and clear descriptions. A collection should help people compare the products it includes. Build meaningful subcategories and link to product pages through normal navigation.

Decide which combinations deserve stable, indexable pages. Align canonicals and links so thousands of near-duplicate variants do not drown out useful collections. Check that filters still work for shoppers and that important products can be discovered without relying on a search box.

Monitor collection impressions, product clicks, and purchases. Refresh sorting and inventory where needed. If visits rise but purchases do not, test product availability, shipping visibility and the match between the query and collection.

checks: Link from navigation to useful collections
Decide which combinations have distinct value
Measure product clicks and orders from category pages

paragraphs: Describe what each service includes, where it is available, and how to make an enquiry. Use separate location pages only when they serve distinct needs. Add real proof and link from useful guides or navigation to the appropriate enquiry page.

Check contact details, hours, services and links. Use an eligible Google Business Profile and accurate categories. Encourage genuine reviews and respond professionally without exposing private customer details.

Track calls and forms alongside confirmed jobs or bookings. Check response time and ask the team which enquiries were relevant. Put clear eligibility and availability on the pages that attract traffic but receive poor-fit calls.

checks: Check name, hours, phone and links
Track accepted jobs as well as form volume

paragraphs: List which work needs doing, who can change the site, and who will own outcomes. An internal team can develop business context over time. An agency may bring several disciplines sooner. A hybrid can pair internal ownership with external specialist support.

Ask who will audit, write, implement and verify fixes. Compare access, reporting, handoff documentation and the practical time needed from developers. Ask for examples of how a recommendation became a live change.

Agree on a baseline and the business actions that matter. Use a regular review to decide which work should stop or expand. Keep control of your domain, analytics and content so you can maintain the work if the relationship changes.

checks: Identify the team responsible for implementation
Keep ownership of domains, analytics and assets
Decide what to continue based on evidence

paragraphs: Search summaries and assistants can answer questions directly, cite a source, or direct someone to another search. A mention, a citation, and a measurable visit are different outcomes. Which ones you can observe depends on the platform.

Use clear definitions, named authors, original examples and source links. Put the answer and supporting evidence near each other. Keep key material accessible and make related pages easy to find. Google recommends standard SEO practices for its AI search features.

Monitor known referrals, customer-reported discovery and selected queries over time. Keep branded search and conversions in the same review so you can distinguish attention from business impact. Record where the measurement is incomplete.

checks: Put original evidence close to claims
Record where referral data is unavailable

paragraphs: Choose repetitive, low-risk questions with approved answers. Define escalation paths for payments, complaints, sensitive information and cases that lack a matching source. Ask support staff which questions are safe to handle automatically.

Organise approved help articles, assign owners, and remove obsolete policies. Have the bot cite the relevant guidance where possible. Limit what user details are retained and test for situations that require an agent to take over.

Use representative conversations and intentionally difficult cases. Review answer accuracy, successful handoffs and customer sentiment. Start with a limited rollout and give support staff a clear way to disable an unreliable workflow.

checks: Test common and risky escalation cases
Roll out gradually and monitor corrections

paragraphs: Collect queries from Search Console, support conversations, paid campaigns and direct customer interviews. Ask AI to group those phrases by need and buying stage. Use its suggestions as hypotheses and check demand with independent data.

Inspect representative search results to see what types of pages serve each task. Merge variants that share intent and separate topics that need different answers. Map each group to an existing page or a clearly defined new one.

Review which pages earn clicks and whether those visitors qualify. Update the map when products change, new questions appear, or search results shift. Keep a record of the evidence used for each change.

checks: Collect genuine queries and customer language
Inspect search results before splitting topics
Attach each intent to an existing or new URL

paragraphs: Use AI for outlines, variations or summaries when helpful. Assign a human owner to verify claims, instructions and source references. Escalate safety-sensitive or technical material to someone with relevant expertise.

Open the primary sources and confirm dates, figures and interface names. Try the steps when producing a tutorial. Replace invented examples with labelled hypothetical scenarios or documented real examples.

Store source notes and identify who will review the page when it becomes outdated. Add useful first-hand details and improve the page when readers flag unclear sections. Review results with the same standards used for other content.

checks: Schedule a human review for material that changes

paragraphs: Choose workflows with clear inputs, outputs and approval points, such as drafting a support reply or routing an enquiry. Write down when the agent should ask for clarification and when it must stop.

Provide access only to what the task needs. Require confirmation for account changes, payments, or external messages where appropriate. Keep a record of decisions and test cases where inputs are incomplete or contradictory.

Compare completed tasks, corrections and escalation rates against your current workflow. A tool that saves drafting time while increasing manual review may be a poor fit. Give the team a documented fallback when automation is unavailable.

checks: Restrict tools and require approvals where needed

paragraphs: Specify working hours, duration, buffer time, holidays and who can take each appointment type. Store availability in the system your team already trusts. Confirm time zone and service requirements before presenting slots.
Treat a proposed slot as tentative until the calendar confirms it. Send confirmation and make changes easy. Route requests involving special requirements or uncertain availability to a person.

Simulate two people choosing the same slot, a cancellation, a time-zone change and an unavailable calendar. Track successful bookings, reschedules, duplicate events and requests that needed human help. Give staff a manual booking path.
Give each builder the same audience, pages, content and required task. Compare how easily the team can change navigation, edit layouts and maintain repeatable pages after the first draft.

Test mobile layout, keyboard navigation, text contrast, headings, forms, metadata and performance. Verify canonical URLs and redirects where relevant. Check export options, ownership and what happens when the subscription ends.

Make a realistic change, such as publishing a new location page or updating shared pricing. Record how much work it takes and whether content can be reviewed before release. Choose based on the whole publishing workflow.

checks: Give each builder the same site brief
Test the rendered page on mobile and with a keyboard
Have a teammate perform a normal update

paragraphs: Use search to answer active questions, paid campaigns to reach specific audiences, and email to follow up with people who agreed to hear from you. Social and partnership content can help people discover what they did not know to search for.
If the goal is more qualified quote requests, decide which offers, customers and locations qualify. Build a clear landing or service page and choose one or two channels you can properly support.

Track completed actions and compare outcomes across channels using consistent definitions. Review the cost and quality of leads, and record what changed before interpreting results. Scale activities once there is evidence they can contribute.

checks: Match the channel to a buying stage
Define who qualifies and why they should act

paragraphs: Check whether the drop affects a few URLs, a section, or the entire domain. Compare similar periods, devices and search types. Note launches, indexing issues, reporting gaps and changes in market demand.

Review queries and top landing pages. Look for outdated content, missing evidence, or an experience that makes the task harder. Check whether pages are indexable and whether a different URL is being surfaced.

Fix specific problems before making site-wide edits. Record the release and review later data using a comparable period. Treat the timing of a search update as a clue, then validate the underlying issue.

checks: Compare comparable periods and affected templates
Check page indexing, demand shifts and recent releases
Record the fix and evaluate after release

paragraphs: List what events you collect, why you need them, and where they are sent. Identify which measurements rely on consent or browser storage. Keep unnecessary personal information out of requests and analytics event parameters.

Use records from orders, CRM and booking systems to understand actual results. Define how you connect campaign data with business outcomes and who can access the reports. Respect consent choices and document any limits in channel-level reporting.

A change in measured conversions can reflect measurement loss, demand, or both. Use consistent definitions and annotate tracking changes. Compare observed data with business outcomes and use controlled tests where you can.

checks: Identify why each event is collected
Reconcile observed trends with business records

paragraphs: Largest Contentful Paint measures how quickly the main content appears. Interaction to Next Paint measures responsiveness to interactions. Cumulative Layout Shift tracks unexpected movement. The good thresholds are LCP at or below 2.5 seconds, INP at or below 200 milliseconds, and CLS at or below 0.1 at the 75th percentile.

Use field data to see what real visitors experience, then reproduce issues with lab tools. A slow hero image, blocked main thread or unsized embed can point to different fixes. Check mobile and desktop separately.

Give images dimensions, reduce unnecessary script work and prioritise the resources the first screen needs. Re-test representative pages and watch field data over time. Measure form completion and usability alongside performance scores.

checks: Check the largest visible element and its loading path
Trace slow interactions and main-thread work
Give media dimensions and stabilise dynamic content

paragraphs: Write down which buyers, needs and locations you serve and what a useful outcome looks like. Set a baseline for leads, purchases and current channel costs before deciding where to invest.

Map the key pages you need and select one or two channels you can support. Write down budget, responsibilities, and what would justify continuing. An initial plan might test one service page, one paid campaign, and follow-up emails to relevant leads.

Compare actual results with the baseline. Look at qualified outcomes and operational capacity, not just traffic. Stop activities that lack a credible path to the goal and use what customers ask to improve future pages and campaigns.

checks: Define a business metric before committing spend
Set a budget, owner and review date
Decide what to continue from evidence

paragraphs: A shopper may first see a product in a social post, search for reviews, and return through a branded query. Build for the questions at each stage and check whether information is consistent across the places that influence the purchase.

Demonstrate the product with real examples, then link to a page that explains price, options, delivery and limitations. Keep availability and specifications consistent with listings and posts that drive visitors.

Track product page engagement, assisted discovery where visible, and completed purchases. Use customer interviews or surveys to identify sources that analytics cannot observe. Make channel decisions with both the data and its gaps in view.

checks: Record the first questions shoppers ask
Compare indirect discovery and completed purchases
